explanation: King Sejong proclaimed Hangul in 1446, more than a century before Shakespeare was born. South Korea celebrates Hangul Day each year on 9 October.

claims.text: King Sejong proclaimed the Hangul alphabet in 1446.
South Korea marks Hangul Day on 9 October.

writerNotes: A neat modern-looking alphabet feels recent, so most players pick Shakespeare; counterintuitive is true. The gap is 118 years. Self-check (9.3): lint run clean; every claim listed with risk at or above the C26 floor and raised where honest; datasets: no pinned dataset covers it; rival test: Hangul was created in 1443 and proclaimed in 1446; either year is more than a century before 1564; volatility evergreen, no time words, nothing depends on knowledge newer than mid-2026; regional: Shakespeare is world-famous and Korea's alphabet is widely known; style: Oxford spelling, straight quotes, no en or em dashes, explanation within 35 words; myths: no match in myths.json; mystery and encore checks: not applicable to a practice item; doubts: none; North Korea marks its own alphabet day on another date, which is why c3 names South Korea
